tables.title: Budget, South Korean Interim Government, Fiscal Year 1947/48
tables.period: Fiscal Year 1947/48; supplemental and total appropriations as of 31 January 1948
footnotes: a/ Approved 89,500,000 won for flood damage; 40,687,733 won for increase in wages; 255,000,000 won for nationalization of ships.
b/ Approved 150 million won for Coast Guards; 547,440,000 won for Constabulary.
c/ Approved 1,132,500 won for printing; 1,581,400 won for Taegu Normal College; 13,579,080 won for Teachers Training; 200,000,000 won for Elementary Schools.
d/ Approved for refugee housing.
e/ Approved for moving office.
f/ Approved for grain inspectors.
g/ Approved 18 million won for bridge construction; 1,879,100 won for reproduction of maps; 105,890,000 won for flood control.
h/ Approved for the development of coal industry.
i/ Approved for billet guard.
j/ Approved for Inchon prison.
k/ Approved for collection of Bank of Chosun notes from refugees.
l/ Approved for purchase of paper.
m/ Approved for purchase of tobacco.
n/ Approved 14,070,460 won for census; 4,215,800 won for Capitol heating; 200,000 won for State affairs; and 3,441,845 won for official gazette; 25,000,000 for national election.
o/ Approved for refugees from China and North Korea.
p/ Approved for housing materials.
q/ Approved for building maintenance.
r/ Approved for summer-grain collection.
s/ Approved for 39 additional employees.

tables.title: Expenditures and Revenues by Months, Unadjusted, South Korean Interim Government, October 1945-December 1947
footnotes: a/ Beginning with April 1946, these figures include Department of Transportation revenues.

b/ Deduction of this amount is due to correction of duplicate accounting of the Normal and Inventory Accounts of the Department of Transportation. Monthly allocation of this amount was not possible. (See Income and Expenditure Table of Department of Transportation, September SKIG ACTIVITIES).
c/ Large increase is due to payment of 3 billion won for summer-grain and rice-collection program in 1946/47 fiscal year.

footnotes: 1/ These balances represent the actual amount of cash held by the financial institutions, excluding the money deposited with other financial institutions.
